name: For Kicks
tagline: You made it up. Now everyone says it.
epigraph: Three coffee beans float on top. They're meant to be flies. It's a long story.
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. One generic sentence ("At every age…"), narrowed at once. Swap test against the Morale Booster (*Anyway*: no plan for a group, no gloom lifted, no list, no rules quoted; the meeting is one clause), the Surrealist (*The Other Berry*: no apology, no hidden swap) and the Trend Setter (*Still Yours*: "made it up", not liked first; near miss on the tagline owned). 4-grams clean against every pour and the closing line; seven collisions fixed in v1 (*Fair Measure*, *Rosetta*, *Beside the First*, *As It Was*, *Any Day*, *Next One's Mine*, explorer-hero's draft). One "I", no we/our/us, no guest pronouns, no strength words; every "his" is McElhone or McIntyre (lint warnings accepted); orgeat explained in plain words (both owners). History 49–50% of yours, 37% of the whole reading. ✓

names_note: **For Kicks**, the room's pick (all three, round 6): what the person does, nonsense for the pleasure of it, with the drink's own name (Cameron's Kick) inside. **Not a Phase** was Wren's round-4 pick; she struck it herself because "it's not a phase" is what many people were told when they came out, and borrowed for silliness it could sting the guests who'd feel it most (both cases in `work/jester-creator/psychologist-alternatives.md`). The two crossed in round 5 (each conceded to the other) and settled in round 6. Also considered: *Fly in It*, *Little Blue Bottlefly* (a bluebottle is a blowfly), *Trap One* (Tomás).
open_items: **Not veto-free: contains nuts** (orgeat, the almond syrup). The room chose Cameron's Kick over the veto-free Boulevardier in round 3 because it is printed in the IBF's own 1927 book; the Boulevardier is credited to Erskine Gwynne, and its Campari is claimed by Explorer and Lover. A guest's own nut veto protects them.

**The float is our inference.** Rodrigues et al. (2003) give roasted beans at 438–755 kg/m³ against water's 1,000; that three beans float on this shaken sour is inferred, not observed on a page. The epigraph ("Three coffee beans float on top") rests on it.

**Harry's proportions read OUT on acid** (the 1927 sixths: 0.64% finished against a floor of 0.76). Our build raises lemon to 22.5 ml and orgeat to 17.5 ml, and y4 owns it ("a little more lemon than his bar's 1927 book does"). Balanced at 15.7% / 7.27 g / 0.88%.

**Coffee look-alikes, owned in Checks:** the beans are a garnish joke, not coffee in the drink. The image stays pale, never an Irish Coffee (*Everybody's*) or an Espresso Martini (Oxford pdf 739, also three beans).

**Kept out on purpose:** "co-founded with McIntyre" (C1), "Harry invented barfly" (L5), the dead-fly sugar lumps (Moss's joke), the IBF rules (Rule 11 included), the war beyond one clause, which family member runs Harry's today (C2), and the orge/barley lead for orgeat (dossier only).

**Stale wording in the dossier:** Wren's Resonance quotes y4's v3 wording ("a little more lemon than the old printed recipe"); reading v4 says "than his bar's 1927 book does" (R1). A working note in the draft ("his book… his sixth") is not guest-facing (Hester, audit v3).
